stories.title: FLX Plans New Fitness Studio in Seattle’s Roosevelt Neighborhood
stories.excerpt: High Street Residential, the residential subsidiary of Trammell Crow Company, announced the signing of a new retail lease on the ground floor of The Ryder, an upcoming 244-unit multifamily community in the Roosevelt neighborhood of Seattle, Washington. FLX, a local Pilates studio, has agreed to take the project’s sole 1,268-square-foot retail space, making it the studio’s second location. The Ryder is expected to be delivered by the end of October 2026, while the studio is expected to open in January 2027. Located at 6716 Roosevelt Way NE, The Ryder is a seven-story, transit-oriented development located one-half block from the Roosevelt Link Light Rail station. The community offers a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom units. The Ryder is also within walking distance to Whole Foods, multiple restaurants and coffee shops. “FLX is exactly the type of tenant we envisioned for The Ryder,” said Alan Cantlin, Principal with TCC in Seattle. “By bringing a locally owned wellness and fitness concept to the property, we’re enhancing the experience not only for our future residents, but also for the broader Seattle community.” The post FLX Plans New Fitness Studio in Seattle’s Roosevelt Neighborhood appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: High Street Residential (TCC) signed FLX Pilates for 1,268 SF ground-floor retail at The Ryder, Seattle Roosevelt.
The Ryder: 244-unit, 7-story TOD opens Oct 2026; half-block from Roosevelt Link Light Rail station.
FLX opening January 2027; second location for local wellness tenant near Whole Foods, restaurants, transit.
stories.summary: High Street Residential leased the sole retail space at The Ryder, a 244-unit transit-oriented apartment community in Seattle's Roosevelt neighborhood, to FLX Pilates (1,268 SF ground floor). The property opens October 2026 adjacent to Roosevelt Link Light Rail; FLX follows in January 2027. The building includes studio, one-, and two-bedroom units within walking distance to retail and dining.
stories.impact: Ground-floor retail lease fills critical amenity gap before unit delivery, signaling developer confidence in Roosevelt neighborhood demand and transit-oriented positioning. FLX's expansion to second location (Seattle Roosevelt submarket) validates emerging neighborhood appeal; retail pre-leasing at 100% occupancy de-risks NOI and improves financing terms, typical for premium TOD projects competing for institutional capital.

stories.title: Freehill Starts Work on 1.6M-SF Houston Warehouse Project
stories.excerpt: Freehill broke ground on Fairbanks Landing, a four-building, 1.64 million-square-foot Class A industrial development in Northwest Houston. The project will be delivered in two phases. Phase I will consist of Buildings 1 and 2, totaling 809,220 square feet, and is scheduled for completion in Q3 2027. Phase II will add Buildings 3 and 4, totaling 834,720 square feet, with delivery expected in Q4 2027. Phase I is being developed by Freehill as a build-to-suit for Power Electronics. JLL’s Ryan Green and Jeff Venghaus represented Power Electronics in the transaction and JLL’s Joseph Berwick, Richard Quarles and Eliza Klein represented Freehill. Berwick, Quarles and Klein are also handling leasing for Phase II on behalf of Freehill. Phase II will include Building 3, spanning 568,080 square feet, and Building 4, totaling 266,640 square feet. Located at 9220 Fairbanks North Houston Road, Fairbanks Landing is positioned near several of Northwest Houston’s major transportation corridors. The post Freehill Starts Work on 1.6M-SF Houston Warehouse Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Freehill broke ground on Fairbanks Landing: 1.64M SF, four-building Class A industrial, Northwest Houston.
Phase I (809K SF, Q3 2027) is build-to-suit for Power Electronics; Phase II (835K SF, Q4 2027) on market.
Located near major transportation corridors on Fairbanks North Houston Road; dual-phase delivery spreads risk.
stories.summary: Freehill began construction on Fairbanks Landing, a 1.64 million-square-foot Class A industrial development in Northwest Houston split into two phases. Phase I (Buildings 1–2, 809K SF) is a build-to-suit for Power Electronics, completing Q3 2027; Phase II (Buildings 3–4, 835K SF) will be marketed and complete Q4 2027. The property sits near key transportation corridors in an industrial submarket.
stories.impact: Build-to-suit anchor (Power Electronics) signals equipment/electronics manufacturing growth in Northwest Houston; full Phase I pre-commitment reduces financing risk. Staggered Phase II delivery strategy allows Freehill to capture pricing momentum and absorb tenant demand across 2027–2028 window, critical as Houston's industrial market tightens due to port activity and supply-chain consolidation near IAH.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges $98M Sale of Medical Campus in Fairfax
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the $97.5 million sale of the Willow Oaks Medical Campus, a 382,850-square-foot, two-building portfolio of medical office buildings located at 8260 and 8280 Willow Oaks Corporate Drive in Fairfax, Virginia. Inova Health System (Moody’s Aa2) acquired the portfolio from Stockdale Capital Partners. Co-Heads of U.S. Medical Office Capital Markets Ben Appel, Jay Miele and Justin Shepherd, Head of Healthcare Debt John Nero, Senior Managing Director Michael Greeley and Associate Directors Ron Ott represented the seller. D.C-area capital markets Executive Managing Directors Jud Ryan and James Cassidy supported the transaction. Each property spans approximately 188,000 square feet and has benefited from multi-million-dollar capital investment initiatives into tenant spaces, common areas and amenities in recent years. Located in the Merrifield submarket, the properties are adjacent to Inova’s headquarters and Inova Fairfax Hospital and benefit from connectivity to the Capital Beltway and Dunn Loring-Merrifield Metro station. The portfolio is also proximate to Tysons, Washington, D.C. and the Mosaic District, a major mixed-use destination offering retail, dining and entertainment. The post Newmark Arranges $98M Sale of Medical Campus in Fairfax appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Inova Health System (Aa2) acquired Willow Oaks Medical Campus for $97.5M from Stockdale Capital Partners.
382,850 SF two-building portfolio in Fairfax, Merrifield submarket; adjacent to Inova HQ and Fairfax Hospital.
Recently capitalized; proximate to Capital Beltway, Dunn Loring-Merrifield Metro, Tysons, Mosaic District.
stories.summary: Newmark arranged the $97.5 million sale of Willow Oaks Medical Campus (382,850 SF, two buildings) in Fairfax's Merrifield submarket to Inova Health System. Properties have received multi-million-dollar capital improvements; located adjacent to Inova's headquarters and hospital, near the Metro and Beltway, close to Tysons and Mosaic District.
stories.impact: Health-system acquisition of medical office adjacent to own hospital signals vertical integration and supply-chain control; indicates stable, long-term occupancy and reduced vacancy risk for Fairfax–Merrifield. However, institutional/nonprofit ownership typically stabilizes rather than catalyzes new multifamily demand—limited direct relevance to apartment development unless Inova headquarters expansion drives workforce growth.

stories.title: Chelsea Warehouse to be Redeveloped into Office Building
stories.excerpt: Jamison Commercial RE and Cahn Family Associates LLC are redeveloping a six-story warehouse and textile building in Manhattan’s West Chelsea Arts District into a boutique office property. Owned and occupied by the Cahn family’s textile business for over 40 years, the building is located at 510-514 W. 27th St., with more than 100 feet of frontage overlooking the High Line. The Cahn family’s business will remain involved in the project and will continue to occupy part of the building for the foreseeable future. In addition to co-developing the project, Jamison Commercial RE will lead sales and leasing through its brokerage division. The planned redevelopment will encompass 51,400 square feet of space, including a ground floor measuring approximately 7,500 square feet, five rentable floors of around 8,500 square feet each, and a 1,400-square-foot penthouse. Davis Architecture and DeSimone Consulting Engineering will design the project, which calls for a comprehensive renovation of the existing structure, from a restored and redesigned facade to a landscaped rooftop outdoor space. A new floor may also be added at the top of the building, subject to governmental approvals. The sponsor plans to create a for-sale commercial condominium and offer the property’s top four floors as a combined acquisition opportunity. The owners also envision the possibility of dividing up the combined space into individual full-floor units and potentially leasing out the available floors. “The combination of direct High Line frontage, full-floor occupancy, outstanding light and views, and a location at the center of the arts district will allow us to create a distinctive boutique property for companies and owners seeking a lasting presence in one of New York’s most important neighborhoods,” said Jamison Weiner, principal of Jamison Commercial RE in a statement. Rendering courtesy of Davis Architecture. The post Chelsea Warehouse to be Redeveloped into Office Building appeared first on Connect
bullets: Jamison Commercial RE and Cahn Family Associates redeveloping textile warehouse to office at 510–514 W. 27th St., Manhattan.
51,400 SF boutique office: ground floor 7,500 SF + five floors ~8,500 SF each + 1,400 SF penthouse; potential top-floor addition.
Cahn family textile business remains as anchor tenant; High Line frontage, 100+ feet visibility in West Chelsea Arts District.
stories.summary: Jamison Commercial RE and Cahn Family Associates are converting a six-story warehouse (owned by the Cahn family textile business for 40+ years) into a 51,400-square-foot boutique office property at 510–514 W. 27th St. in Manhattan's West Chelsea Arts District. Design includes ground retail (7,500 SF), five office floors (~8,500 SF each), and penthouse (1,400 SF), with possible additional floor subject to approval. The Cahn family will remain as tenant.
stories.impact: Warehouse-to-office conversion in West Chelsea reflects tight Manhattan office supply and continued capital chasing trophy adaptive-reuse in high-barrier-to-entry neighborhoods. Limited direct multifamily impact; however, if redeveloped West Chelsea office absorption accelerates, subsequent residential rents in Chelsea/Flatiron may benefit from workforce concentration—but this development alone is small-scale and creative office, not driver of residential demand.

stories.title: Private Equity Firm Sentinel Capital Expands to 35K SF at One Vanderbilt
stories.excerpt: Private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners has expanded to 34,737 square feet at One Vanderbilt. The deal gives Sentinel an additional 7,134 square feet of office space on a portion of the tower’s 54th floor, according to a Monday announcement by landlord SL Green Realty. The move brings Sentinel’s total footprint at the trophy high-rise to 34,737 square feet. The lease term and asking rent for the expansion were not disclosed, but SL Green’s Steven Durels told Commercial Observer in February that rents in the building ranged from $250 to “well over $300” per square foot. In-house brokers represented SL Green in the transaction, while Newmark’s Brian Waterman and David Waterman negotiated on behalf of Sentinel Capital. The 1.7 million-square-foot tower, located at 1 Vanderbilt Avenue just west of Grand Central Terminal, remains 100 percent leased, according to SL Green. Law firm Greenberg Traurig recently signed a 10.5-year deal for another 33,477 square feet at the high-rise, CO reported this month, bringing its total footprint to 133,365 square feet. Other office tenants at One Vanderbilt include TD Bank, investment management firm Carlyle Group, alternative investment firm Oak Hill Advisors and SL Green itself. Spokespeople for Sentinel Capital and Newmark did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sentinel Capital Partners expanded to 34,737 SF total at One Vanderbilt (SL Green); new 7,134 SF on 54th floor.
Asking rents $250–$300+ per SF per SL Green; 1.7M SF tower at 1 Vanderbilt Ave remains 100% leased.
Newmark represented Sentinel; SL Green's Durels noted robust demand for trophy Manhattan office space.
stories.summary: Private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners expanded at One Vanderbilt, adding 7,134 square feet on the 54th floor to bring total footprint to 34,737 SF. Lease terms and rent not disclosed, but SL Green's asking rents range from $250 to over $300 per square foot. The 1.7 million-square-foot trophy tower near Grand Central Terminal remains 100% leased.
stories.impact: 100% occupancy at trophy Manhattan office (One Vanderbilt, Greenberg Traurig expansion, Sentinel expansion) signals institutional capital flowing into elite NYC office and suggests continued white-collar job concentration in Manhattan. However, office expansion does not drive multifamily demand unless accompanied by labor force growth or wage inflation—most trophy office tenants are already Manhattan-based or relocating within the metro, not net new job creation.

stories.title: McCombs Eyeing Tax Breaks for San Antonio Mixed-Use Venture
stories.excerpt: McCombs Enterprises is seeking to capture tax revenue to fund the infrastructure needs of a mixed-use project the company is proposing. The developer estimates the project will require roughly $43.6 million in public infrastructure improvements and says any reimbursement would come through a proposed TIRZ cutout. McCombs would pay for half of those costs. The San Antonio Business Journal reports plans for the site include retail and office space between Pearl, the San Antonio Museum of Art and the River Walk. McCombs has said the development would cost around $395 million. The completed project could generate more than $160 million in city property and sales tax revenue over time, excluding taxes paid to the San Antonio Independent School District. Staff said they expect to return to the committee in October. Any incentive package would require approval from the Midtown TIRZ board before going to city council. The post McCombs Eyeing Tax Breaks for San Antonio Mixed-Use Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: McCombs Enterprises seeking tax-increment financing (TIRZ cutout) for $395M San Antonio mixed-use project.
Developer estimates $43.6M in public infrastructure needs; McCombs will pay half; project completion could generate $160M+ tax revenue.
Mixed-use retail and office between Pearl, SAMA, River Walk; October committee return expected.
stories.summary: McCombs Enterprises is pursuing a Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone (TIRZ) incentive package for a mixed-use development in San Antonio's downtown-adjacent Pearl/Museum/River Walk corridor. The $395 million project requires roughly $43.6 million in public infrastructure; McCombs will fund half, seeking reimbursement via TIRZ cutout. Over time, the project could generate $160 million in city property and sales tax revenue (excluding school district taxes). Staff expected to return in October.
stories.impact: TIRZ financing for major mixed-use development signals San Antonio city support and may reduce cost of capital, improving development feasibility. Retail/office-heavy mix in high-traffic corridor indicates office-first positioning; limited direct residential component mentioned, so limited demand impact on multifamily. If project succeeds, downstream residential demand may follow worker and visitor concentration, but McCombs' focus here appears primarily retail/office, not apartment development.

stories.title: Hedge Fund Castle Hook Takes Penthouse Office at Related’s 625 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: New York-based hedge fund manager Castle Hook Partners has landed the penthouse office lease at Related Companies’ upcoming 625 Madison Avenue tower. According to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Monday, Castle Hook inked a deal for the entire 52nd and 53rd floors of the planned 53-story development. The asking rent was not disclosed, but there’s no doubt that Castle Hook paid a premium. Related is seeking rents of up to $400 per square foot for the tower’s upper floors, the Wall Street Journal reported in July. The 15-year lease term includes options to renew an additional 10 years. Castle Hook currently lists its headquarters at BXP’s 767 Fifth Avenue, known as the General Motors Building. It is unknown whether the lease with Related represents a relocation or an expansion for the firm. A spokesperson for Related declined to comment on the deal, and the Castle Hook team did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Castle Hook’s deal follows global investment firm General Atlantic’s 152,000-square-foot commitment at 625 Madison Avenue, announced earlier this month. The future anchor tenant is slated to occupy five floors. Private equity firm Veritas Capital also appeared to secure 92,743 square feet at the development, according to Colliers’ August Manhattan office snapshot report. Ralph Lauren’s Polo Bar is also in talks to relocate to Related’s tower, according to WSJ, signaling the iconic restaurant’s potential relocation from 1 East 55th Street. Related’s Philippe Visser signed the mid-September deal on behalf of the developer. David Rogers, an executive officer at Castle Hook, signed for the tenant. It is unclear whether outside brokers were involved in the transaction. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hedge fund Castle Hook Partners leased entire 52nd–53rd floors (penthouse) at Related's 625 Madison Avenue, NYC.
15-year lease with 10-year renewal options; asking rents up to $400/SF for upper floors; unknown if relocation or expansion.
Related's 53-story tower remains fully leased; follows Greenberg Traurig 33,477 SF deal.
stories.summary: Hedge fund Castle Hook Partners signed a 15-year lease (with 10-year renewal options) for the penthouse (52nd–53rd floors) at Related Companies' 625 Madison Avenue, a planned 53-story tower. Asking rents for upper floors reach $400 per square foot. Castle Hook currently occupies BXP's 767 Fifth Avenue (GM Building); unclear if this is a relocation or expansion. The tower remains 100% leased.
stories.impact: Trophy Manhattan office at $400/SF reflects continued premium institutional demand and tight Class A supply; however, Castle Hook's move (unknown if net new or internal shuffle) provides no direct signal of labor-force expansion in Manhattan. Like other trophy office leasing, signals capital confidence in high-barrier office but does not directly drive multifamily demand unless paired with employment growth.

stories.title: Elysee Investments Buys Shopping Center Near Waterford Business District for $28M
stories.excerpt: Elysee Investments paid $28 million for a relatively new, fully leased shopping center near Miami’s Waterford Business District. Called Blue Lagoon Shoppes, the 29,205-square-foot property at 1101 Northwest 57th Avenue sits inside the business district, just south of Miami International Airport. The 250-acre Waterford Business District is home to the headquarters of major companies such as Burger King, Subway and Lennar Homes. Blue Lagoon Shoppes’ 13 tenants include Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera Bread, Jersey Mike’s, BankUnited and Panda Express. Mario Borda of Borda Commercial Real Estate represented Elysee Investments, while Avison Young’s John K. Crotty, David Duckworth and Brian C. de la Fé represented the seller, Keystone Holdings Group. “The strongest-performing retail investments today are the ones that combine essential-service tenancy with irreplaceable locations,” Avison Young’s de la Fé said in a statement. “Blue Lagoon Shoppes delivers both through its national-credit tenant roster, full occupancy and strong location.” Keystone Holdings Group completed the 2.4-acre asset in 2021. Elysee Investments specializes in retail properties in Miami-Dade and Broward counties. In 2024, the investor bought a 6.7-acre, grocery store-anchored property in Aventura for $48 million. Representatives for Elysee Investments and Keystone Holdings Group did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Elysee Investments bought Blue Lagoon Shoppes for $28M: 29,205 SF, fully leased, near Miami Waterford Business District.
Tenants include Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera, Jersey Mike's, BankUnited, Panda Express; 13 national credits; completed 2021.
Located 1101 NW 57th Ave, just south of Miami International Airport; 250-acre district anchored by Burger King, Subway, Lennar HQ.
stories.summary: Elysee Investments acquired Blue Lagoon Shoppes, a 29,205-square-foot, fully-leased shopping center near Miami's Waterford Business District, for $28 million. Built by Keystone Holdings Group in 2021, the property includes 13 national-credit tenants (Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera, Jersey Mike's, BankUnited, Panda Express). Located at 1101 NW 57th Avenue south of Miami International Airport, the center sits within the 250-acre Waterford Business District, home to Burger King, Subway, and Lennar Homes headquarters.
stories.impact: Fully leased, essential-service retail in enterprise/corporate submarket (Waterford Business District near IAH) signals consistent anchor-tenant demand and investor appetite for stabilized retail near corporate clusters. However, retail acquisition itself does not directly create residential demand unless Waterford BD workforce expands—watch for office/logistics expansion from Burger King, Subway, or Lennar as proxy for future apartment demand in South Miami/Waterford submarkets.

stories.title: Brixmor Property Group, Everview Partners Acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34B
stories.excerpt: One of the largest owners of shopping centers in the U.S. just got bigger. Brixmor Property Group, a $9 billion publicly traded real estate investment trust (REIT) and holder of a portfolio of 346 shopping centers spanning more than 63 million square feet, announced Monday that it has partnered with Everview Partners to acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34 billion. Slate Grocery REIT has a portfolio of 115 grocery-anchored, open-air retail centers that together comprise 15.7 million square feet of real estate. Under the terms of the deal, Brixmor will acquire 23 shopping centers in Florida, Georgia and the two Carolinas for $636 million, but will form an institutional joint venture with Everview Partners and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority that will acquire the remaining 92 assets from Slate Grocery REIT for $1.71 billion. Brian Finnegan, Brixmor’s CEO and president, told Commercial Observer on Monday that his firm was motivated to finalize the deal with Everview Partners after seeing a large amount of institutional capital enter the open-air, grocery-anchored retail space in recent years and “validate the asset class.” “This opportunity to get 23 assets that we’re purchasing ourselves, as part of a broader portfolio where we can leverage the platform, just made a lot of sense to bring in a partner like Everview,” he said. “[The new portfolio] is in markets we know really well with a lot of growth potential, redevelopment opportunities right out the gate, and significant mark-to-market rent opportunities, as well. Brixmor plans to grow “long-standing grocer relationships” and capitalize on numerous “remerchandising, redevelopment, and outparcel opportunities,” according to a release. bullets: Brixmor Property Group and Everview Partners acquired Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34B; 115 assets, 15.7M SF grocery-anchored retail.
Brixmor acquiring 23 centers in FL, GA, Carolinas for $636M; Brixmor-Everview-ADIA JV acquiring 92 assets for $1.71B.
Deal reflects institutional capital influx into grocery-anchored, open-air retail; Brixmor now 369 centers, ~80M SF total.
stories.summary: Brixmor Property Group partnered with Everview Partners and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority to acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34 billion, adding 115 grocery-anchored open-air retail centers (15.7M SF). Brixmor purchases 23 centers in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas directly ($636M); a joint venture of Brixmor, Everview, and ADIA acquires the remaining 92 assets ($1.71B). This expands Brixmor's portfolio to 369 centers spanning ~80 million square feet.
stories.impact: Consolidation and institutional capital surge into grocery-anchored retail signals investor confidence in essentials-driven retail resilience. For multifamily developers: elevated institutional appetite for stabilized, non-discretionary retail (near existing residential concentrations) may reduce available ground-floor retail opportunities in new apartment projects and raise anchor-tenant cost; conversely, grocery-focused retail near apartment communities supports higher rents and occupancy. Key markets (FL, GA, Carolinas) overlap high-growth residential markets—monitor for retail bidding wars.

stories.title: Solidcore Signs Lease for Fitness Studio at 1695 Second Avenue on Upper East Side
stories.excerpt: A strength training brand has signed a retail lease on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Solidcore, a national fitness chain that offers high-intensity workouts, took the entire retail component of Alchemy-ABR Investment Partners’ 1695 Second Avenue, a new 23-story, 51-unit residential building on East 88th Street, according to landlord broker JLL. JLL did not disclose the square footage of the lease, but plans for the building — dubbed the Langdon — laid out 2,507 square feet for the retail space, YIMBY New York reported in late 2024. Asking rent and the length of the lease were also not disclosed, but the average asking rent for the nearby retail corridor of Third Avenue from East 72nd to East 60th streets was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a CBRE report. “We worked closely with JLL to identify a retail tenant that would complement the Langdon’s residential experience and reflect the quality of the property,” Jedd Horn, director of capital markets for Alchemy-ABR, said in a statement. “Solidcore is an ideal fit. Its loyal following, premium positioning and distinctive fitness offering will provide a valuable amenity for our residents while bringing a highly sought-after brand to this part of the Upper East Side.” Matthew Schuss and Jesse Wolff of JLL negotiated on behalf of the landlord, while Sean Young of Sabre negotiated on behalf of Solidcore. Young did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Today’s best retail leasing strategies are built around concepts that complement a property and contribute something meaningful to the surrounding neighborhood,” Schuss said in a statement. “Solidcore has cultivated an exceptionally loyal following and will bring energy, convenience and a highly sought-after fitness experience to the Langdon.” Virginia-based Solidcore offers high-intensity but low-impact strength training at more than 100 studios across the U.S. The company has 18 locations in New York City, with the majority in Man
bullets: Solidcore signed retail lease for entire component at Alchemy-ABR's 1695 Second Avenue (The Langdon), Upper East Side, NYC.
Building: 23-story, 51-unit residential; retail space ~2,507 SF; nearby Third Ave corridor averaging $252/SF (Q2 2026).
Solidcore: national high-intensity fitness chain; Upper East Side retail corridor signaling premium tenant demand.
stories.summary: Solidcore, a national high-intensity strength-training fitness brand, leased the entire retail component of Alchemy-ABR Investment Partners' 1695 Second Avenue (The Langdon), a new 23-story, 51-unit residential building on East 88th Street. The retail space is approximately 2,507 square feet; lease term and rent not disclosed, though nearby Third Avenue retail averaged $252 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Solidcore's flagship Upper East Side retail commitment in luxury residential building signals strong fitness/wellness tenant demand in high-income multifamily submarkets. Ground-floor retail pre-lease at 100% occupancy improves NOI and financing on small-format residential; fitness anchors attract and retain high-net-worth residents, supporting premium rents. Upper East Side retail at $250+/SF suggests continued capital concentration in Manhattan luxury residential; relevant for aspirational developer positioning but limited to trophy markets.
